title: The Loday realization of the associahedron: its hyperplane, its facets and its face lattice
author: Naruki Masuda; Hugh Thomas; Andy Tonks; Bruno Vallette
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.142
difficulty_reason: The proposition collects five properties of the weighted Loday realization K_omega of the associahedron: the hyperplane containing it, its description by half-spaces with equality exactly on decomposable trees, the fact that this hyperplane-and-half-space system cuts the polytope out, the identification of the face lattice with the lattice of planar trees, and the product decomposition of any face (statement lines 670-691). The proof's substance is in clauses (3) to (5): clause (3) requires showing that the equations defining a vertex have nested or disjoint intervals, which is done by deriving a strict inequality that contradicts the defining half-spaces (proof lines 699-731), clause (4) then reads the face lattice off the facet description of clause (2), and clause (5) exhibits the explicit isomorphism Theta putting a product of two smaller Loday realizations onto a facet (proof lines 738-753). Clauses (1) and (2) are dismissed by the author as straightforward from the definition, and both dismissals are kept verbatim in the counted span; they are not where the item's obligation lies, since the decisive statement is the combinatorial description of the polytope, which is proved. H2.
